description: Active energy is at least 100 times the reported CO2 quantity.
explanation: CO2 is an emissions estimate derived from electricity use, and the reported units and rounding place the emissions quantity well below active energy on this scale.

description: Elapsed seconds since midnight plus active energy is nonnegative.
explanation: NSM is a nonnegative daily-clock quantity and active energy is a nonnegative consumption quantity.

description: The daily-clock upper bound plus lagging reactive energy is at least NSM.
explanation: NSM is defined on the daily clock through 86399 seconds; lagging reactive energy is nonnegative, so adding it cannot violate the stated clock upper bound.

description: The daily-clock upper bound plus leading reactive energy is at least NSM.
explanation: NSM is defined on the daily clock through 86399 seconds; leading reactive energy is nonnegative, so adding it cannot violate the stated clock upper bound.

description: Active energy plus estimated emissions is nonnegative.
explanation: Both active electricity consumption and estimated emissions represent nonnegative interval quantities.

description: Elapsed seconds since midnight plus estimated emissions is nonnegative.
explanation: Both NSM and the emissions estimate are nonnegative interval quantities by definition.

description: Elapsed seconds since midnight plus lagging power factor is nonnegative.
explanation: NSM is a nonnegative daily-clock value and lagging power factor is expressed on a nonnegative percentage scale.

description: Elapsed seconds since midnight plus leading power factor is nonnegative.
explanation: NSM is a nonnegative daily-clock value and leading power factor is expressed on a nonnegative percentage scale.

description: Estimated emissions plus lagging reactive energy is nonnegative.
explanation: Both estimated emissions and lagging reactive energy are nonnegative interval magnitudes.

description: Estimated emissions plus leading reactive energy is nonnegative.
explanation: Both estimated emissions and leading reactive energy are nonnegative interval magnitudes.

description: The daily-clock upper bound plus estimated emissions is at least NSM.
explanation: NSM is at most 86399 seconds and estimated emissions are nonnegative.

description: The daily-clock upper bound plus active energy is at least NSM.
explanation: NSM is at most 86399 seconds and active interval consumption is nonnegative.

description: The daily-clock upper bound plus lagging power factor is at least NSM.
explanation: NSM is at most 86399 seconds and lagging power factor is nonnegative.

description: The daily-clock upper bound plus leading power factor is at least NSM.
explanation: NSM is at most 86399 seconds and leading power factor is nonnegative.

description: Elapsed seconds since midnight plus lagging reactive energy is nonnegative.
explanation: NSM is a nonnegative daily-clock quantity and lagging reactive energy is a nonnegative interval magnitude.

description: Elapsed seconds since midnight plus leading reactive energy is nonnegative.
explanation: NSM is nonnegative by its daily-clock definition and leading reactive energy is a nonnegative interval magnitude.

description: Estimated emissions plus lagging power factor is nonnegative.
explanation: The emissions estimate is a nonnegative interval quantity and the lagging power factor is reported on a nonnegative percentage scale.

description: Estimated emissions plus leading power factor is nonnegative.
explanation: The emissions estimate is nonnegative and the leading power factor is expressed as a nonnegative percentage measurement.
